Title: Cloud Practitioner Certification reschedule because technical problems | AWS re:Post
I recently had a problem when trying to do my certification exam and I'd like to know if someone else had a problem when taking a photo of their IDs with the check-in page of Person VUE. It happens that today I had scheduled my AWS Cloud Practitioner Certification and at the moment of the check-in after I took the photo my ID, the proctor told me my ID was not clear. So I retook it and was still blurry but that just happened with their check-in page, not with my native camera. I was neither able to focus the part that was blurry and for that reason, my exam was cancelled and I'm looking forward to know if I can reschedule it without having to pay extra fees (accordingly to Person VUE customer service it was my fault just to have one ID and also because of my "faulty" device). It's really frustrating and I'd like to know what can I do and if someone had a similar situation. The problem it's that I invested part of my savings to achieve this and it's a shame to loose it. Thanks in advance for your help! Since re:Post is a community forum site, we cannot provide refunds for AWS exams. Therefore, it may be a good idea to contact Pearson VUE from the URL below. Also, although there is no guarantee that they will respond, it may be a good idea to consult with us about the issues you are facing using the inquiry form regarding the AWS certification exam below. I already talked with them at they just said NO. I contacted Amazon Customer Service but they told me I have to contact Person VUE and wait five days if I didn't get any response. It's frustrating because I need this certificate before the end of the month. Thanks for your prompt response. I hope AWS or Pearson VUE will support this. results.title: AWS SES Bounce and Complaint Rates: Review and Pause Limits
results.content:
## If your account is under review.

You can still send. AWS is giving you time to fix the cause. The notice goes to the email address of your AWS account, which may differ from the address you send from, so check that inbox.

### 1. Stop the sending that caused it

If you can, pause sending until you know the cause. Sending on unchanged makes the numbers worse.

### 2. Find the cause

A bought, rented or old list; a sign-up form that accepts mistyped addresses; mail that readers did not ask for. Removing the bad addresses alone does not satisfy AWS; it wants the process fixed.

### 3. Reply to AWS's case

In the AWS Console, open Support Center and reply to the case AWS opened. Say what caused it, list the changes you have already made (not plans), and how they stop it happening again. [...] ## What counts toward each rate.

### Bounces

Only hard bounces (permanent failures such as "address does not exist") to domains you have not verified. A full mailbox, a temporary failure, or a bounce caused by a blocked IP address does not count.

### Complaints

A complaint is a reader pressing "Report spam". The rate in your SES console counts only complaints from email providers that send feedback to AWS. Complaints that readers or providers send to AWS directly stay out of that number, and they still count against you: AWS can review your account on them alone.

### Spam traps

Addresses that exist only to catch careless senders, often old addresses that have bounced for a long time. AWS does not say how many hits it takes; even a few hurt.

## If your account is under review. [...] ## If your sending is paused.

The steps are the same: find the cause, fix it, then reply to the case in Support Center. Your SES Account dashboard shows Paused or Healthy. AWS can pause without a review first when the problem is serious, or when the same problem has put your account under review before.

A pause also affects other AWS services that send messages: AWS may refuse quota increases for Amazon SNS until your SES sending is restored.

## How to stay well below the limits.

### Send only to people who asked

Never buy, rent or share lists. Use double opt-in: a confirmation email that a new subscriber must click.

### Stop mailing an address the moment it hard bounces or complains

Every time. A hard-bounced address left on a list can later become a spam trap.
